checked_sources.evidence: Opened; IAU lines 48–65 defines official bounded constellation areas and abbreviations, while line 145 lists Lacerta / Lac.

Opened; NASA lines 255–270 describes BL Lac's bright disk and Earth-oriented jets, IXPE with radio/optical telescopes, polarization discrimination, and electron-photon Compton scattering for the X-rays.

articles.finding: The IAU supports Lacerta/Lac and the area-versus-line-figure distinction. NASA supports BL Lac as a blazar with a supermassive black hole, bright disk and Earth-oriented jet, the IXPE/radio/optical campaign, and the electron-photon/Compton explanation for the X-rays. The article does not confuse a map direction with stellar membership.

checked_sources.evidence: Opened; IAU lines 53–65 supports the bounded-sky-area account and line 132 lists Delphinus / Del.

Opened; NASA lines 295–322 identifies Caldwell 42/NGC 7006 in Delphinus, defines its globular-cluster structure, distinguishes background galaxies, and explains the visible-versus-infrared dust effect.

articles.finding: The source supports NGC 7006/Caldwell 42 in Delphinus as a globular cluster; its dense, roughly spherical and mutually gravitationally bound stellar system; fuzzier extended background galaxies; and dust making visible light dimmer while infrared passes better. The self-check uses those distinctions correctly.

articles.finding: NASA supports M33 as a spiral galaxy in Triangulum at about 3 million light-years, Hubble's central-region/inner-arm mosaic, visible millions of stars and hundreds of clusters, blue rapid-star-birth areas, NGC 604 as a major star-forming region, and the Cepheid/variable-star evidence that M33 is outside the Milky Way.

articles.finding: NASA supports M27 as a planetary nebula in Vulpecula more than 1,200 ly away; the historical planet-like naming; ejecta of an old dying star; and its processed colour channels (oxygen blue, hydrogen green, sulfur/nitrogen red). The text accurately labels those as data visualisation.
